positions.blocker: Is one build per physical disk (CX-984-002) the real ceiling, and should a third slot or a higher cap exist on C:?
positions.decision: Keep two slots and CX-984-002 tonight. No third slot, no higher cap, no RAM disk, no USB HDD slot. Shrink holds first (positions below). Morning question for the Operator, only if median wait is still over 5 minutes after those cuts: may `cargo check` class commands run beside a holder on C:? Separate purchase question: an NVMe drive for build targets.
positions.why: The queue is real: 13.5 builder-hours waited in two days, and a 24 s job waited 648 s. But the cause is heavy tails in a FIFO lock: per-sha 55% of lock time, and runs over 300 s are 67% of the rest. Half of it is removable by habit. The machine is disk-bound, not CPU-bound: one round on C: already shows CPU 16% and disk queue about 20. A second link-heavy build on a SATA QLC disk with a 78 GB cache and about 172 MB/s after it would add writes to the bottleneck. The rule is the Operator's Codex text, and the harness refused the lead's relaxation of HSK-ART-005 today, so the lead should not assume it can relax this one. A USB HDD slot would need a CX-984-014 grant and a cold target; a RAM disk needs a driver install and competes with the memory gate that held R59.
positions.risk: Holds do not shrink as estimated and the two slots stay the limit through the night, about 7.5 lock-hours in the window.
positions.control: Record median wait and lock-hours per lane every 2 hours from the run logs' `acquired after` lines, reading only logs written since the last reading. If median wait is over 5 minutes at T+4 h, cut to 6 builders rather than add slots.
positions.proven_wrong_if: Once the Operator allows it, an A/B of the same harness-view viewer build alone and as two concurrent builds on C: shows the pair each under 1.3x the solo time with commit free over 40 GB. Then a second C: slot is right and this decision should be reversed.
positions.unblocks: More parallel builders without a Codex change

positions.blocker: How builders iterate cheaply, and which steps need the lock
positions.decision: Three-step ladder in every brief. (1) `cargo check -p <crate> --tests`, in one hold with anything else due. (2) Focused runs name targets: `cargo nextest run -p <crate> --test <file>`. Never use `-E binary(...)` or lane-check `--tests` to narrow a build: they narrow the run, not the link. (3) One bundled run after review. Keep every cargo command under the lock as the wrapper does today. Do not take test execution out of the lock tonight (authority member's GOV-LANE-CHECK-LOCK-1).
positions.why: Test execution is 4.7% of builder lock time and about 9% of a round, so moving it gains little and adds wall-clock test failures under load, plus an edit to a script that running lanes source. The link is the cost. The log with `-E binary(diag_sink)` listed 87 binaries and skipped 85, so all were built. A focused run of 28 tests took 935 s. lane-check's own `--tests` becomes one `-E` filter, so it has the same cost. Nextest documents `--test` as selecting the target.
positions.risk: A `--test` run misses a sibling test the change breaks, and that surfaces later at the bundled run or the round.
positions.control: The bundled run still covers the suites of the crates the lane edits. Check of the harness pair [viewer] stays. Use one canonical -p and --features form per crate, so targets are not rebuilt under another feature identity (cargo research free_now).
positions.proven_wrong_if: A logged `--test` run on harness rebuilds as many binaries as the package run, or red and focus hours do not fall by at least 40% against 2.94 h per the same mix of lanes.
positions.unblocks: Short holds that stop queuing behind 37-minute bundles

positions.decision: A lane's bundled run is the whole suite of the crates it edits, except harness and harness-view: for those two, only named `--test` targets unless the lane edits that crate's src. Rule 4b suites such as package stay. Drop clippy over dependents with the existing STUDIO_LANE_CHECK_NO_DEPENDENTS=1 only if the lane is not editing a public signature. The scope reports' 'WHOLE harness-view' lines are cut to this for engine lanes. Budget: 5 commits, one bundled run, two failed runs then a fresh diagnostics agent.
positions.why: The harness pair is 88 to 98% of test-binary bytes and 74 to 80% of round build time. Bundles of 700 to 2248 s are almost all that link. The round links them anyway, and the Operator asked for minimal testing with rounds as the proof.
positions.risk: More breaks reach the round instead of the lane, each costing a fix and a verdict from the budget of 3.
positions.control: Compile check of the harness pair at the tip stays in the push gate. Code-check and red-team read before the bundled run. A lane that changes behaviour the Viewer uses names those targets in its brief.
positions.proven_wrong_if: R60 fails more than 2 lanes on harness or harness-view tests the lane's narrowed run skipped. Then restore whole suites for folio and session lanes only.
positions.unblocks: Harness link time off D: for every engine lane

positions.decision: Tip only, as workflow item 11 says, and skip it entirely when the push gate reports a disjoint rebase. Squash a lane to at most 3 commits before the tip check. Take the round-time audit's 5 dropped units in round-features, which also shrinks per-sha because it reads the same matrix.
positions.why: It was the largest single consumer of the lock and found 2 failures in about 63 runs. Those failures are compile errors the tip check or the round's default build would also find, unless they sit on a non-tip commit, which rounds do not judge. Repeats after rebases cost hours.
positions.risk: An intermediate commit does not compile, so bisecting is harder (the origin of F-R48-4 and F-R49-1).
positions.control: RED COMMITS rule stays for what is pushed: squash non-compiling reds before the push. A failed trunk check names the landing, which is enough for tonight's scale.
positions.proven_wrong_if: The next round's build fails on a commit that a skipped per-sha would have caught, more than once in the night.
positions.unblocks: About 10 of 20.7 lock-hours per two working days (ESTIMATE)

positions.blocker: The push slot: one lane pushing at a time, with holds during rounds
positions.decision: Abolish the slot and the round push hold. Git's non-force push is already an atomic compare-and-swap on the branch. A lane lands by: fetch, rebase, `tools/lead/push_gate.py` (new, read-only, `cargo metadata --no-deps`, runs unlocked), then the guarded push. Gate rule: let O be the crates origin changed since the lane's old base and L the crates the lane changed. If no crate in O has a dependency path to or from a crate in L, the rebase is disjoint: no build, run the lane's new tests only if it has not run them, push. Otherwise run the tip check on the intersecting closure, then push. On rejection, repeat. No lead release step. A trunk check on a clean tree (`cargo check --workspace --tests` plus harness [viewer]) runs after every 3 landings or 2 hours, and before any round freeze.
positions.why: CX-VAL-001 freezes one candidate and says later commits queue for the next round, so a push during a round cannot touch the round. Today's PUSH HOLD on STUDIO-R59 is a habit: SMB-CONTROLS-EGUI-GATE-1 is sitting at phase push_hold for a round expected to run hours. Conflict analysis is the field's way to avoid a queue: independent changes do not wait on each other. A merge queue is the heavier form, and with one machine it would serialise the same builds.
positions.risk: A trunk break lands, or a same-file semantic clash passes a clean textual rebase. The 2026-10-21 incident shows pushes are dangerous when scripted loosely. A repair of a round FAIL rebases over newer work. I did not find a recorded reason for the round hold in Codex; one may exist in the validator's practice (UNVERIFIED).
positions.control: PUSH SAFETY text stays verbatim, no force, no delete. Dependency path test includes dev-dependencies. Same-file edits always count as intersecting. A red trunk check stops new landings on that closure only, and the owning lane fixes forward. The R59 validator gets told in its next message that origin may move beyond c4d06841 while it works, and judges only the candidate.
positions.proven_wrong_if: Two or more trunk breaks in one night, or the validator shows a verdict depended on origin not moving. Then bring back a slot for lanes that touch folio or session only.
positions.unblocks: Many landings an hour, and the egui gate lane now

positions.blocker: Round policy and keeping CX-VAL-011 honest
positions.decision: After R59: no round until a real wave. Freeze R60 at 8 READY lanes or at T+5.5 h, whichever is first, never for fewer than 6 READY unless a HIGH fix is waiting. R60 is FULL, as already due. Land everything that forces a full round before that freeze: steward sync, new dependency versions, the matrix cut. Then keep the lockfile set and `.config` still until the next due FULL. Never narrow a selection by hand; round-select computes it. Count every round in the third-round rule. Report READY as unjudged in every summary to the Operator.
positions.why: A round is worth its cost in lanes judged per hour. R58 spent 3 h 48 on one claim, and R55 about 3 h on 3. Scoped costs about the same as FULL whenever the harness family is in the closure, so the third-round rule costs little; timing is what matters. A root input change costs a canary too (R54-canary 1 h 57), so fold all such changes into one sync. Authority member already drops WF3-007's 8-hour half.
positions.risk: Up to about 7 hours of unjudged lanes. A systematic error, such as the externals classifier failing three rounds in one class, spreads across a whole wave before any verdict.
positions.control: Review before every bundled run. Trunk check before freeze. If two lanes' reviewers report the same failure class, write it into the common brief that day (lessons). A HIGH fix may trigger a scoped round early, which then counts toward the third-round rule.
positions.proven_wrong_if: R60 fails more than a quarter of its READY lanes. Then the batch was too large: freeze at 4 to 5 lanes.
positions.unblocks: C: as a builder slot for about 2.75 hours between rounds

Jobs: audit says the disks may be the limit, and os error 1455 is on record. Merging changes test ids, so claim mappings need migrating, and it would collide with every harness lane during the wave.

positions.control: Retained sets still cover the negative branches: desktop+viewer lacks media, audio-batch+audio-device lacks os-encode. Rebuild the old matrix once at WP boundary (CX-EXEC-008). The commit names the matrix change so the validator can challenge it. Changing it is a checked-in commit (CX-VAL-007), never a runtime override.

positions.decision: Split work by the map below. Rules: (a) one lane at a time on each hot file in tier 1; everyone else adds a new module and one registration line. (b) Only one lane at a time adds a field to a widely-literal struct, and it lands fast; new text attributes go into one new struct behind one new field, so later lanes do not sweep again. (c) Engine lanes reach a document through session and typed commands, and leave Viewer exposure to one exposure lane per domain per 2 hours. (d) Land RF-01 as one short mechanical lane, with no other lane in view/mod.rs, shell.rs, hosted.rs during it. (e) New GUI crates per the shell and Vulkan members' plans go first in parallel, since they conflict with nothing. (f) Order among folio lanes: first ready lands; others take only the tip check and their new tests.

Most lib.rs collisions are module and re-export lines. Struct literals make one field a many-file edit. The first wave already has three lanes in harness cli.rs and harness-core harness.rs.

positions.blocker: Agents: how many, and which model and effort
positions.decision: Peak 8 builders (5 on D:, 3 on C:), 1 validator, 1 steward, at most 4 read-only reviewers at once, 2 scenario or designer agents. While a round holds C:, C: lanes write code and take only cargo check holds under about 2 minutes in round gaps; no bundled run or cleanup on C:. Each lane gets one review pass before its bundled run: separate code-check and red-team agents for folio schema, session, save-path, or harness-level lanes; one combined agent doing both for leaf lanes of at most 3 commits. Re-review only on a HIGH finding. Update WF3-002, which still says 5 builders.
positions.why: Agents waiting on a lock cost wall-clock, not disk (lessons); the stale-base and review load is what grows. Disk capacity is about 2 lanes an hour, so more than 8 builders only lengthens waits. R59's lane needed a third pre-review before it was safe, which shows reads catch what tests miss, but repeated passes are the busy work the Operator excluded.
positions.risk: Lower-effort builders produce more rework. Combined reviews miss what separate adversarial reads catch. Reviewer backlog delays bundled runs.
positions.control: Raise effort on any builder whose first review has a HIGH finding. If a reviewer queue passes 30 minutes, the builder continues on its next slice; the review still precedes its bundled run.
positions.proven_wrong_if: More than a third of lanes get a HIGH finding on review or FAIL in R60 from the medium-effort group. Then raise that group to high.

positions.control: One probe lane, queued like any other, under 45 lock-minutes in total or it stops. Round proof unchanged (CX-VAL-007). STUDIO_DEBUG opt-out stays for failure work, per the research.
positions.proven_wrong_if: V3 saves under 25% of relink time on harness-view viewer. Then drop it and keep debug line tables.
positions.unblocks: Second-half capacity and C: free space
